findings.reason: a worker implementing §5 will find the audit cannot see an outside path, so the section must say what carries one into the audit before its deliverable can be built.
findings.text: §5 states "the write-time audit and promotion still refuse different paths for that kind", but at §1's head the write-time audit (`_orientation_substance` → `_committed_scope`) and promotion (`promotion_checks` → `_scope_paths_at_head` over `cumulative.paths`) both derive their path set from git commits, and a commit only ever carries repository-relative paths, so the outside-repository branch of `_declaration_needed_kind` is unreachable from either surface — the plan is reconciling a divergence neither surface can observe

findings.reason: the done-when measures nothing until it names the input that carries an outside path (the manifest's changed_paths, not commits), so the node cannot close on one test verdict.
findings.text: §5's first case ("a run whose commits touch a path outside its repository is refused by the write-time audit and by promotion") and its negative control ("promotion accepts the outside-repository path the audit refuses") cannot be produced or failed: no commit can touch a path outside its repository, and the fourth case compounds it by requiring that same unreachable audit case be asserted through the audit's own verdict
